items.title: Education Session - Community Safety Zones and Municipal Speed Cameras
notes:
Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation Services, provided a presentation looking at the importance of lowering vehicle speeds and how the program is designed to lower vehicle speeds. A copy of the presentation was attached to the agenda. He stressed that excessive speed is a factor in 25% of fatal crashes and that vehicle speed cameras have demonstrated that they are effective at lowering speeds. D. Spooner provided an overview of what has been learned from the current program and the benefits of moving to the administrative penalties program from the current Provincial Offences Act (POA) court, stressing that it is more effective and scalable. He noted that revenue exceeding operating costs will be directed to the road safety reserve fund and will be reported to Council on an annual basis.

Responding to questions, D. Spooner explained that any municipality that is using the administrative penalties program will have the fine amounts doubled in those areas because it is a requirement under provincial regulations. He stressed that the administrative penalties program will allow for local decisions on compassion for financial hardship.

D. Spooner spoke to the ability for an area municipality to opt out of the program, noting that cameras could still be installed on Regional roads in that municipality. He explained that because the program is scalable it would be possible to reduce the size of the expansion or move cameras to municipalities that are participating in the program. D. Spooner stressed that the existing POA court administration does not have ability to expand to deal with the expected volume of tickets.
